Rapid Entire Body Assessment
Risk score from whole-body posture, load, coupling and activity.

Risk score from arm, wrist, neck and trunk posture plus muscle use and force.
Static workstation jobs loading the arms and neck: assembly line, desk work, cashier.
A side-on frame; observation of force, static posture or repetition.
Legs are assessed roughly; one side only.
Ovako Working Posture Analysing System

A rough posture class is enough; angle measurement not required.

Not valid for one-handed or seated lifting, pushing-pulling, carrying or unstable floors.
Composite Lifting Index
Composite index of lifts with different loads, heights and frequencies.
Jobs where the same person does mixed lifting at different shelf levels or with different cartons: palletising, shelf loading.
NIOSH measurements and lifts per minute for each sub-task.
Tasks must be in the same duration category; FM is interpolated for intermediate frequencies.

Load score from daily repetitions/time/distance plus load, posture and conditions.
Manual handling including carrying and holding; a quick estimate when measurement is not possible.
Daily count, time or distance; effective load; posture and condition class.
2001 version; BAuA published an extended version in 2019. A rough screening tool.
Moore-Garg Strain Index
Hand-wrist risk index from force, duration, repetition, wrist posture, speed and daily duration.
Repetitive hand and wrist work: assembly, packing, cutting, screwdriving, meat processing.
An observation for each multiplier; estimates of cycle time and exertion time.
Hand, wrist and elbow only; for a single task.

ACGIH Hand Activity Threshold Limit Value
Compares hand activity level and peak force with the threshold limit value (TLV) and action limit.
Repetitive hand work; a second opinion to the Strain Index.
Exertions per minute and duty cycle, or a HAL rating; a 0–10 peak force rating.
For mono-task hand work of 4 hours or more a day; shoulder and elbow not covered.

Recommended surface height based on elbow height and type of work, and the difference from the current surface.

8-hour equivalent exposure from different levels and durations, with the regulatory thresholds.
Noisy areas such as presses, compressors, cutting, assembly lines.
dB(A) measurement and duration for each job or area; peak dB(C) if any.

Nordic questionnaire
Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ)
Pain/discomfort in nine body regions over the last 12 months and the last 7 days.
Collecting complaints systematically, setting analysis priorities, before-after comparison.
A short interview with each worker (about 5 minutes).

Not a diagnostic tool; contains health information, use a code instead of a name.
Liberty Mutual pushing, pulling and carrying equations
Calculates the maximum acceptable push-pull force or carrying weight for the task conditions and what percentage of the population finds the measured value acceptable.
Pushing-pulling carts, pallet trucks, roller conveyors; manual carrying.
Hand height, distance, frequency; initial and sustained force (N) with a force gauge, or the weight carried.
Outside the valid ranges the result comes with a warning; an 8-hour day and a moderate climate are assumed. The publication only defines the 75% female target.
Key Indicator Method – Lifting, Holding, Carrying (2019)
Separate load scores for women and men from daily count, load, handling, posture, unfavourable conditions and organisation.
Common in Germany/EU; detailed screening of manual handling jobs.
Daily count, effective load, the posture pictogram on the official form, condition observations.
The posture weighting must be chosen from the pictograms on the official form; linear interpolation is used for intermediate counts; female load scores above 30–35 and 40 kg were extrapolated as 100.
Key Indicator Method – Pushing and Pulling (BAuA LMM-ZS, 2019)
Push-pull load score from equipment type and total weight, daily distance, floor, conditions, equipment condition, posture and organisation.
Manual pushing-pulling of carts, pallet trucks, sack trucks, containers, overhead rail systems or overhead cranes; without a force gauge.
Equipment type, total weight including the equipment, daily distance or time, observation of floor and equipment.
Rolling or dragging without equipment, powered vehicles and special carts with support wheels are out of scope. The floor score is taken as 0 for overhead systems.
Lifting Fatigue Failure Tool
Probability of a high-risk job from the fatigue damage that all lifts during the day accumulate on the lower back.
Many lifts at different weights and distances; comparing the effect of improvements.
Load, horizontal distance from the spine to the load and daily count for each lift type.
Moments above 100 N·m should be interpreted carefully; one published example probability (25%) is not reproduced with these coefficients.
Distal Upper Extremity Tool (DUET)
Cumulative damage and probability of disorders for the hand-wrist-elbow from exertion difficulty (OMNI-RES) and daily repetitions.
Repetitive hand work; several movements of different difficulty.
A 0–10 difficulty rating and daily count for each type of movement.
The web version of the tool may have updated the coefficients in later versions; the published paper values were used.
Measurement / observation
Revised Strain Index (2017)
A continuous risk index from force (%MVC), frequency, exertion duration, wrist angle and daily duration.
Repetitive hand work; more precise than the original Strain Index when numerical measurements are available.
%MVC (or Borg × 10), exertions per minute, seconds per exertion, wrist angle, hours per day.
For a single task; the multi-task composite (COSI/CUSI) rules were not added.
OCRA checklist (classic version)
Combines recovery, frequency, force, posture and additional factor scores with a duration multiplier.
Repetitive upper-limb work on assembly and packing lines; the ISO 11228-3 approach.
Break pattern, action frequency, force durations, shoulder-elbow-wrist-grip observation, net repetitive time.
The classic version was applied; the tables of the 2011 revised version could not be verified. The sources contain no fully worked example.
Rapid Office Strain Assessment
Office risk score from 1 to 10 from the chair, screen, phone, mouse and keyboard.
Computer work; a scored, comparable office assessment.
A choice for each item while looking at the workstation, plus daily usage times.
Only the action level of 5 is published; the extra point for depth adjustment could not be verified.
